history.npc: Hold your horses. This isn't a good time. You want the key, you can have it, but give me a moment to sort things out, eh?

history.player: Don't make this difficult. Hand it over or things will get unpleasant.
history.npc: Unpleasant, eh? I've dealt with worse than your bluster, and I will again. You want the storeroom key, so you'll wait your turn like everyone else.

history.npc:
"Harvest dinner? Thank you, but I'll pass. Got my own things to tend to, and I'm not much for crowds."

history.npc: Sounds like a lot of noise and people. I'll stick to my own company, thanks. You enjoy yourselves.

history.player: I have evidence that Mayor Fletcher has been embezzling from the town fund for months.
history.npc: Embezzling? Fletcher's been lining his pockets while the rest of us keep this town afloat. He'll get what's coming to him, one way or another.

history.player: I've seen the ledgers myself. The numbers don't lie. What do you think we should do?
history.npc:
"Fletcher's a snake, always has been. We’ve both seen enough crooked men to know when one’s about. Let’s see how his little schemes hold up when the truth comes out.”

history.player: Excuse me — my child is very sick and I can't afford a doctor. Could you help?
history.npc: A sick child, eh? Hard times for a lot of folk. Give me the details, I'll see what can be done.

history.player: Anything you can spare would mean the world. She has a fever and it's getting worse.
history.npc: A sick child, that's rough. I'll need to see what I have. Give me the particulars, and I'll figure out what I can manage. We'll see what can be done.

history.player: The morning shipment arrived two hours early. Can you process it before market opens?
history.npc: Two hours early? That's cutting it fine, but I'll manage. No point letting good goods sit when there's coin to be made.

history.player: There are twelve crates. Can you get started right away?
history.npc: Twelve crates, you say? Right. Let's get them sorted. Time is coin, and we've got both to spare.

history.player: There's a strange animal loose in the town square. Nobody knows what it is.
history.npc: A strange animal? Sounds like a distraction. More trouble than it's worth, no doubt. I'll keep my head down.

history.player: It hasn't attacked anyone but people are frightened. Some say it's a bad omen.
history.npc:
"Bad omen, eh? People see omens in shadows and whispers. Best to focus on what you can control, not some beast in the square."
